messages:
maya: Quick bring-up notes for marlin-9b-int4 onboarding — cost vs quality snapshot. TL;DR: int4 looks attractive for most chat/FAQ workloads: ~2.8x cheaper than fp16 at steady state, small quality hit on long-form generation. Recommended initial plan: 5% canary for customer-facing chat, route >512 token requests to fp16 fallback, enable prefix KV caching.

maya: scorecard (sample slice: customer support + long-form docs):
```
metric                 | fp16 (baseline) | int4  | delta
------------------------------------------------
avg latency (ms)       | 85              | 92    | +7
tokens/sec             | 2100            | 2000  | -4.8%
P@1 (faq)              | 0.842           | 0.838 | -0.5%
ROUGE-L (long)         | 0.655           | 0.649 | -0.9%
cost / 1M tokens ($)   | 58.0            | 20.7  | -64%
```

maya: Calculation notes: cost estimate uses live throughput median across instances, GPU runtime cost = $3.2/hr (reserved worker mix), amortized infra = +12%, serving overheads included. We applied a 1.1x safety margin.

rohit: Where did the 1M token cost come from? did you include batching gains and cache hit assumptions?

maya: yes — baseline includes batching at 8 for async chat traffic and KV-prefix cache hit ~18% (derived from last 2 weeks). If we pessimistically drop cache hits to 5% int4 cost goes to ~$24 / 1M tokens.

ellie: I ran a micro-benchmark with batch=1..16 on same model on p4d. Key notes:
- batch 1 tail p95 latency = 180ms (int4) vs 165ms (fp16)
- batch 8 median throughput gains flatten after seq_len>1024
- noticed hallucination spikes on instruction-heavy QA for 3/200 prompts (small but real)

maya: thanks. sounds like product should avoid routing critical instruction QA → int4 for now. do we have a short eval slice for that?

ellie: created eval slice: `instr-heavy-qa-2026-03` (200 prompts). int4 reproducible fail count = 3, fp16 = 0. pushed results to the scorecard linked in the doc.

rohit: operational ask: for canary, propose routing 100% of short chats (<256 tokens) to int4 and keep long tasks on fp16. Also add automated quality watchdog: fail if rolling window accuracy delta > 0.8% absolute on the instr-heavy slice. Thoughts?

maya: agree. plan:
- canary 5% traffic, but shape by seq_len: short chats preferentially targeted
- monitoring: per-slice delta + token-level perplexity drift + synthetic prompt set every 5m
- fallback: immediate reroute to fp16 if alert fires twice in 10m

deploy-bot: :robot_face: Canary job scheduled: marlin-9b-int4 canary v0.1 -> 2026-03-15T18:10Z, targets: 5% traffic (short chat slice). Monitoring hooks created: instr-heavy-qa-2026-03, chat-latency-slice.

maya: next steps for GTN/product handoff: create a short one-pager with unit econ (two columns: short-chat vs long-form) + example customer scenarios. I'll draft and tag @rohit and @ellie for review.

rohit: I'll prepare the unit-econ sheet and include sensitivity rows for cache hit 5/15/25% and GPU price +-20%.

ellie: I'll add the micro-benchmark artifacts and the failing prompts to the eval repo.

maya: sweet. aiming for canary start + 48h observation window before widening. will post status updates here. :thumbsup:
